relevance_note: National survey with patient-level tables of 54 HA20 patients: 'All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3' (Supplementary Tables 1-2 give each patient's genotype and features).
method_note: Patient-level data come only from Supplementary Tables 1-3 (HTML tables in the Markdown); main-text Tables 1-4 are group-level. A Python script in my scratch directory transcribed Supplementary Tables 1 and 2 by character offset and cut every table span directly from the file; I checked its output row by row against the tables, and all feature mappings were chosen by me. Labels: the paper's systematic form 'P1'-'P54' (Supplementary Tables 1-3) is used for every patient although the text says 'patient N'. Scope: the 54 surveyed patients; four relatives described in relation to a patient (mother of P3 and father of P18, both with low-level somatic TNFAIP3 mosaicism; father of P38 with HA20 and grandmother of P15 with suspected HA20, both described for malignant lymphoma); and two excluded mosaic carriers in the Supplementary Material (unnamed person 1, c.806-1G>T at 22%; unnamed person 2, p.Q760X at 14%), plus the two symptomatic family members of unnamed person 2 who did not carry p.Q760X (labelled 'family member of unnamed person 2' and '... 2 2'). No rows for the three asymptomatic heterozygous carriers, the 20 excluded missense cases (Supplementary Table 6 lists variants, not people) or the pedigree-only individuals, which are mentioned only as counts or in figures. No variant row for father of P38 or grandmother of P15, because the paper ties no TNFAIP3 variant to them explicitly. Symbols: Supplementary Table 2 never defines '−' or '-' (hyphen), so every such cell is 'not reported' and gives no excluded rows. Its '+' counts match Table 2 for fever (46) and oral ulcer (42). '+' cells were read as present, with the column header quoted as a second span. Cutaneous entries plus P10's BCG dermatitis give 27, matching Table 2. Checklist policy: 'Intestinal symptoms +' alone was not taken as GI ulcers or inflammation. That item is observed only where the initial diagnosis names intestinal BD, IBD or Crohn's disease (not 'Crohn's disease susp'), and for P3 ('gastrointestinal lesions' with inflammation, Discussion). Lymphadenitis was not counted as lymphadenopathy. Eyelid conjunctival aphthae (P1) and posterior iris adhesions (P54) were not counted as ocular inflammation. Graves' disease (P17) was not counted as autoimmune thyroiditis. Suspected diagnoses ('AIH susp' for P53, 'PFAPA (suspected)' for P11, 'BD susp', 'CAPS susp') were not recorded as observed. Other initial-diagnosis labels (BD, PFAPA, JIA, etc.) were not recorded as features. The group statements naming the 5 CNS patients and the 3 pulmonary patients were not used to exclude those features for anyone else. 'Asymptomatic' (mosaic relatives) was not expanded into checklist exclusions. Ethnicity 'Japanese' for all except P51 rests on the statement that 53 were Japanese and P51 Vietnamese. Encoding: table spans keep the Markdown's '>' entity and the supplement text keeps '\>', while values give the printed '>'. Multi-line cells are rendered with a single space in values. Contradictions: (1) P49's variant is 'c.2088+1G>A' in Supplementary Table 1 and the minigene section but 'c.2099 + 1G>A' in the main text. The table string was recorded. (2) The supplement lists the splice-site variant 'c.986+1G>T' where it describes generating the constructs, but 'c.986+1G>C' in the minigene results and in Supplementary Table 1 (P50). (3) The genital ulcer '+' count in Supplementary Table 2 is 20, but Table 2 says 19. (4) The Supplementary Table 2 legend defines 'HS, Hashimoto's disease' but the table uses 'HD'. HD was read as Hashimoto's disease because 8 HD entries match 'Hashimoto's disease (8)'. (5) Table 2 lists acute encephalopathy (3) and headache (5), but the per-patient table shows 1 and 4. (6) In Supplementary Table 3, P48's ADA absorbance 0.44 is marked Negative, although the stated cut-off is >0.102. (7) The main text says HA20 was confirmed via functional analysis of every variant, but the supplement excludes large deletions and known variants from the reporter assays, so this is recorded only as the diagnosis basis. Main-text citations (3), (5) and (20) refer to a reference list that is not in the Markdown. Supplementary Table 1's 'reference' column appears to use the Supplementary Material list (refs 7-24 are cited nowhere else). source_reference_in_review is 'not reported' for the 54 patients, who are described first-hand; their per-patient reference entries are: P1 (7,8); P2 (7,8); P3 (7,9); P4 (7,10); P5 (blank); P6 (7,11); P7 (7); P8 (7); P9 (7); P10 (7); P11 (7); P12 (7); P13 (7,12); P14 (7,12); P15 (7); P16 (7,13); P17 (7); P18 (7,14); P19 (4,7); P20 (2); P21 (blank); P22 (15); P23 (15); P24 (16); P25 (17); P26 (17); P27 (17); P28 (18); P29 (19); P30 (19); P31 (20); P32 (blank); P33 (blank); P34 (blank); P35 (blank); P36 (4); P37 (4); P38 (21); P39 (22); P40 (22); P41 (blank); P42 (blank); P43 (blank); P44 (blank); P45 (blank); P46 (blank); P47 (23); P48 (24); P49 (blank); P50 (4); P51 (blank); P52 (blank); P53 (blank); P54 (blank).
